messages.author: 9be5ae75921aca4a
messages.subject: HMM prior on stationary probability
parts:
Hi,

I have a HMM model that looks as below. The component mixtures are such that they have increasing variance. However, I would like to put a prior on the long term (stationary) probability such that it doesn't spend too long on the K-th state (say <10% of the time). 

I know that the eigenvector of the transition matrix (theta) is the stationary probability. Any thoughts on how I can go about creating a prior/ putting restrictions on this?

Thanks,
Sachin

data {
int<lower=0> N; //Number of observations
int<lower=0> K; // number of categories
real y[N]; // estimated treatment effects
}
parameters {
simplex[K] theta[K];  // transit probs <-NEED TO PUT PRIOR ON THIS
real mu[K];
positive_ordered sigma[K];
}
model {
real acc[K];
real lg_alpha[N,K];

// Forward step
for (k in 1:K){
    mu[k] ~ normal(0.0,10.0);
    lg_alpha[1,k] <- normal_log(y[1],mu[k], sigma[k]);
}
for (t in 2:N) {
    for (k in 1:K) {
        for (j in 1:K)
            acc[j] <- lg_alpha[t-1,j] + log(theta[j,k]) + normal_log(y[t],mu[k],sigma[k]);
        lg_alpha[t,k] <- log_sum_exp(acc);
    }
}
increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(lg_alpha[N]));
}

messages.subject: HMM prior on stationary probability
parts: You can make the eigenvalues and eigenvectors parameters and theta goes into transformed parameters.  The eigenvalues should have priors between -1 and 1 and each column of the right (?) Eigenvectors can be a simplex. If you use a sort on the eigenvalues parameters you can assure the first is the largest and the corresponding eigenvector can be the simplex that corresponds to the stationary distribution you want to put priors on.  I've thought about this more for VAR models than for HMM so I'm not sure I have all the details right.

That is why they call "Page rank" the billion-dollar
eigenvector. It was originally a discrete particle
MCMC algorithm to compute the stationary distribution of
a Markov model based on a simple model of random-walk
web crawling.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] HMM prior on stationary probability
parts:
You could put beta priors on the components of the firs
eigenvector, but it's not going to be efficient.

What happens when you fit the model without this constraint?
Where does the knowledge that the K-th state should be less
than 10% of the total come from?

And is this for a single state K (I can't tell with the caps)?

You could try putting a prior on the first eigenvector, but
I'm not sure how best to formulate it, and it's going to be hugely
expensive to compute given that we don't have a way to just
extract the first eigenvector.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] HMM prior on stationary probability
parts:
Our eigenvector function returns a matrix of all the eigenvectors
rather than just the first eigenvector. It's an O(N^3) algorithm
for an N x N matrix. There are more efficient algorithms for
finding just the first eigenvector.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] HMM prior on stationary probability
parts:
Shouldn’t the transition matrix be built up generatively?
I.e. using simplices for each row of the eigenvector
matrix, Q, and positive values for the eigenvalues, lambda,
then reconstructing the transition matrix as Q * lambda * Q^{T}?

Then you can put whatever priors you want on the eigenvectors
and eigenvalues directly.

Besides, doing anything else would require a Jacobian of the
eigendecomposition which is super ugly (it’s used in the softabs
RHMC implementation).
